grades.quote: The RISC-V page table hardware connects these two kinds of addresses, by mapping each virtual address to a physical address.
grades.reason: Explains virtual-to-physical mapping, but not why sparse gaps need no physical storage.

grades.quote: In order to allow processes to use this kind of _sparse address space_ without wastefully occupying a corresponding amount of physical memory, the operating system simply doesn’t provide physical address mappings for virtual addresses in the gaps.
grades.reason: Directly explains that unused gaps in the address range are not backed by physical memory.

grades.quote: Recall that virtual memory address spaces are generally quite sparse: only a small fraction of the possible page numbers actually have translations to page frames.
grades.reason: Directly explains that only a small fraction of the virtual range maps to physical page frames.

grades.quote: For those you want to store, you allocate page frames, wherever in memory is convenient. For those you don’t want to store, you don’t allocate page frames at all.
grades.reason: Illustrates selective physical backing using a virtually stored page table, rather than directly addressing an application's sparse address space.
